title: Reinspection Request
tips: Name the specific items in dispute — don't just ask for "another look." Attach documentation in the same message.

title: Reinspection Follow-Up
body:
Hi {{adjuster_name}},

Following up on the reinspection request I sent on {{original_request_date}} for {{client_name}} ({{claim_number}}). Do you have a date we can lock in? Let me know if you need anything else from us to get it scheduled.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: Ask for a firm date, not just confirmation it's "in progress."

title: Appraisal Demand Follow-Up
body:
Hi {{adjuster_name}},

Following up on the appraisal demand we sent on {{demand_date}} for {{client_name}} ({{claim_number}}). Can you confirm your selected appraiser so we can move forward? Let me know if there's anything outstanding on our end.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: Keep this short — you're just confirming their appraiser is named and the clock is moving.

title: Adjuster Follow-Up (General)
body:
Hi {{adjuster_name}},

Following up on {{claim_number}} for {{client_name}} — specifically on {{what_you_need}}. It's been {{time_elapsed}} since my last message. Can you give me an update, or let me know if you need anything further from us?

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: State exactly what you're waiting on and how long it's been — this makes the pattern clear if you need to escalate later.

title: Appraiser Follow-Up
body:
Hi {{appraiser_name}},

Checking in on {{claim_number}} for {{client_name}}. It's been about {{time_elapsed}} since our last update — is there anything new on your end, or anything you need from us to keep things moving?

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: 2-3 weeks without an update is the standard trigger for this follow-up during active appraisal.

title: Documentation Request (to client or vendor)
tips: Explain why you need it, briefly — people respond faster to a request that makes sense to them.

title: Client Follow-Up (General)
body:
Hi {{client_name}},

Just following up on {{what_you_need}} for your claim ({{claim_number}}). We're ready to move forward once we have this — let me know if you have any questions or if now's not a good time, and we can find something that works.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: Keep it warm, not just a repeat of the same ask — invite a response.

title: Client Explanation of Appraisal
body:
Hi {{client_name}},

I wanted to walk you through the next step in your claim. Because {{carrier_name}}'s estimate and ours are far enough apart, we're going to invoke something called appraisal — it's a process built into your policy for exactly this kind of disagreement.

Here's how it works: each side picks an independent appraiser to review the damage, and if the two appraisers don't agree, a neutral third person called an umpire settles the difference. This isn't a sign anything has gone wrong — it's a normal, contractual way to resolve a disagreement on scope or pricing.

I'll keep you updated at each step. Do you have any questions before we move forward?

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: Avoid promising a specific timeline or outcome — keep it to the mechanics and next steps.

title: Client Stalled-Claim Message
body:
Hi {{client_name}},

I know this claim has been taking longer than either of us would like. Here's where things actually stand: {{current_status}}. Here's what we're doing next: {{next_step}}.

I'll keep you posted as soon as there's an update — feel free to reach out anytime with questions.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: Lead with facts, not just reassurance — clients respond well to knowing exactly where things stand.

title: Internal Escalation Message
body:
Hi {{lead_name}},

I need your input on {{claim_number}} ({{client_name}}). Quick summary: {{situation_summary}}.

What we've tried so far: {{what_tried}}.

What I need from you: {{specific_ask}}.

Happy to hop on a call if that's faster.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: Lead with the specific ask — a lead reading a dozen of these a week will thank you for not burying it.

title: Reinspection Request + Itemized Dispute Notice (State Farm 10-Day)
tips: Use this instead of the plain Reinspection Request on every State Farm file. It starts the 10-day clock on the same day as the reinspection request, so a next-day reinspection denial costs nothing. 1) List EVERY disputed line separately. A bare estimate attachment is the main way State Farm argues the notice wasn't itemized. 2) Get proof of receipt: portal upload confirmation, the adjuster's reply, or certified mail. Save it to the Contractors Cloud project. 3) Calendar the appraisal demand for day 12 after confirmed receipt (2-day buffer over the 10-day minimum).

title: Appraisal Demand (10-Day-Compliant, State Farm)
body:
Hi {{adjuster_name}},

Re: {{client_name}} — Claim {{claim_number}} — Policy {{policy_number}} — Date of loss {{date_of_loss}}

On behalf of the named insured(s), {{client_name}}, written demand is made for appraisal under the Appraisal condition of the policy.

Pre-appraisal notice: Written, itemized documentation of the specific dispute as to the amount of the loss, identifying each disputed item separately, was provided to State Farm on {{notice_sent_date}} and received on {{notice_received_date}} (proof of receipt attached). That is {{days_elapsed}} days before this demand, which meets the requirement of at least 10 days' notice.

Amount in dispute: {{total_difference}}. The itemized comparison is attached again for reference.

The insured's appraiser is {{appraiser_name}}, {{appraiser_company}}, {{appraiser_phone}}, {{appraiser_email}}.

Please name State Farm's appraiser within the time the policy allows and confirm receipt of this demand by reply.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}

Attachments: proof of receipt of the itemized notice (dated {{notice_received_date}}), itemized comparison, insured's signed authorization
tips: Send only when days_elapsed is 10 or more, counted from State Farm's RECEIPT of the notice, not our send date. We standardize on day 12 or later. Always attach the proof of receipt: a court has sided with State Farm where the insured couldn't show State Farm got the estimate before the demand. Have the demand signed or authorized by the insured per our standard appraisal process. If you're re-serving after a 'premature' rejection, add one line: 'This demand supersedes our demand dated {{prior_demand_date}}.'

title: Premature-Demand Rejection Response (State Farm 10-Day)
body:
Hi {{adjuster_name}},

Re: {{client_name}} — Claim {{claim_number}}

We received your {{rejection_date}} letter declining appraisal on the grounds that our demand was made less than 10 days after itemized notice of the dispute. The record shows otherwise:

- {{notice_received_date}}: State Farm received our written, itemized documentation of the disputed items (proof attached).
- {{demand_date}}: Appraisal demanded, {{days_elapsed}} days later.

State Farm's denial of our reinspection request on {{reinspection_denial_date}} does not change when the itemized notice was received. The Appraisal condition measures the 10 days from that notice, not from any reinspection decision.

Please withdraw the rejection and name State Farm's appraiser. If State Farm maintains its position, please identify in writing the specific policy language and the specific requirement you say was not met, so we can review it with the insured.

Thanks,
{{your_name}}
tips: Use this only when our demand was actually compliant: 10+ days after PROVABLE receipt of an itemized dispute. If it wasn't, don't argue. Re-serve with the 10-Day-Compliant Appraisal Demand, which is faster. Getting the 'specific policy language' answer in writing is what you need for escalation or a DOI complaint if State Farm digs in.
